newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope tells Brazil president to continue reforms.
newsitem.headline: Pope tells Brazil president to continue reforms.

text.p: Pope John Paul called for respect for indigenous peoples and fairer wealth distribution on Friday when he received Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso at the Vatican.

The Pope, who spoke with Cardoso privately for 40 minutes, said in a speech afterwards that while recent reforms were praiseworthy, efforts still had to be made to improve wealth distribution in Brazil.
"A fair distribution of wealth (is carried out) with attention to and solidarity with the most disadvantaged and needy people," the 76-year-old Polish Pope said.
He said the Roman Catholic Church in Brazil, South America's largest country and the world's largest Catholic country, was committed to helping the needy included Brazil's indigenous population.

"Respect for indigenous peoples, commitment to agrarian reform carried out according to existing laws and protection of the environment -- all justify ever more courageous initiatives capable of improving democracy," the Polish Pontiff said.
The Pope, due to visit Brazil for the third time next October, also denounced abortion and called for a larger role for women in Brazilian society.
Cardoso, who arrived in Italy last Monday on a five-day visit and is due to leave later on Friday, told the Pope that Brazil was the world's "most Catholic country".

Cardoso, a 65-year-old leftist sociologist turned liberal free-marketeer, has won widespread praise since taking office last January, enacting reforms that brought down inflation to just 10 percent in 1996 and helped lift some 13 million Brazilians above the poverty line.
